title: Object/blob storage & file systems (S3-style, chunking, replication, durability)
relevance: High — almost every media/file HLD (Instagram, YouTube, Dropbox, Pastebin, chat attachments) expects S3/blob + metadata DB + CDN/presigned uploads; Amazon and infra-heavy loops also probe "design S3" durability/chunking.
company_notes: Campus/intern HLD: S3 + CDN + metadata DB is table stakes for paste/newsfeed/Instagram/YouTube/chat/e-commerce images; presigned upload and multipart differentiate. Mid (1–4 YOE): design Dropbox/YouTube/S3 with chunking, ECC vs replication, hot prefixes, consistency, lifecycle — Amazon, Meta, Google, Uber, Flipkart, Cohesity, Databricks. Near-universal for media/files; full object-store build less common than using S3 correctly, but Amazon/infra loops go deeper.

phases.goal: Establish block vs file vs object, the S3 bucket/key model, and the metadata vs data plane split.

must_hit.point: Block storage is raw volumes for DBs/VMs (low latency, mutable); file storage is hierarchical NFS/SMB with shared POSIX-ish semantics; object storage is flat bucket+key with HTTP API and immutable whole-object writes for unstructured blobs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate cleanly maps EBS-like volumes vs NFS/SMB dirs vs S3-style blobs and says when each wins.

must_hit.point: S3 model is bucket + key → object (bytes + metadata); "folders" are key prefixes; app DB stores pointers/URLs/metadata and must not use multi-MB DB BLOBs as the primary store.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says prefixes not real directories, and keeps large bodies out of Postgres/MySQL.

must_hit.point: Two planes: a hot metadata plane (sharded KV/DB: key → size, etag, chunk map, ACLs) and a colder data plane (disk nodes holding chunks) that scale and fail independently.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates metadata service from chunk/disk fleet and notes independent scaling.

must_hit.point: Durability means bytes are not lost forever; availability means you can read now — S3 markets 11 nines (99.999999999%) durability via multi-device/AZ redundancy and integrity checks, not 100% uptime.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly distinguishes durability from availability and cites 11 nines without calling it an uptime SLA.

probes: Contrast block, file, and object storage and sketch how an app should store a photo: where do bytes live vs where does metadata live?

hints.1: Think about what a DB volume needs versus a shared filesystem versus a blob HTTP API.
hints.2: Name bucket/key, prefixes, and a separate metadata DB pointing at the object.
hints.3: Block = EBS/DB/VM disks; file = NFS/SMB dirs; object = flat key, immutable PUT; never put multi-MB JPEG bodies in MySQL — metadata row + object store.

phases.goal: Explain multipart/chunking, direct client upload via presigned URLs, placement, consistency, and integrity checks.

must_hit.point: Multipart upload: initiate → upload parts in parallel with per-part retry → complete (server assembles); abort cleans up; best practice for large objects ≥100 MB; enables resume and bounded retry cost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks initiate/parts/complete/abort and mentions parallel upload and retrying one part, with ≥100 MB as the large-object practice.

must_hit.point: Prefer presigned URLs (or CDN) so clients upload/download directly to the blob store; app servers stay control-plane for auth and metadata — avoid proxying GB through the API tier.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws client → presigned PUT/GET to S3; app only grants short-lived access and writes metadata.

must_hit.point: Modern S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT, overwrite, and DELETE; historically LIST could lag — state the consistency assumption for your design.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says strong RAWW for object mutate/delete and does not assume every blob store behaves identically.

must_hit.point: Place chunks across disks, racks, and AZs (optionally regions via CRR) so disk/AZ loss does not mean user-visible data loss; geo-replication is a separate latency/cost/compliance choice.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions multi-AZ spread and treats cross-region as a product decision, not automatic.

must_hit.point: Integrity uses per-part/object checksums (CRC/MD5/SHA), scrubbing/bit-rot detection, plus versioning or object lock for accidental delete recovery.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names checksums plus background scrubbing and versioning/lock as delete-protection.

probes: Walk multipart upload for a large video on a flaky network, then explain why the client should use a presigned URL instead of streaming bytes through your app servers.

hints.1: Separate control plane (auth/metadata) from the byte path.
hints.2: Sequence initiate → parallel parts → complete/abort, and say who signs the URL.
hints.3: ≥100 MB → multipart with per-part retry; orphaned parts cleaned on abort; short-lived presigned PUT so app never proxies GB.

phases.goal: Force a clear choice between replication and erasure coding, and between hot serving patterns and cold durability cost.

must_hit.point: 3× replication is simple and fast to repair but costs ~3× storage; erasure coding (e.g. Reed–Solomon/LRC) reconstructs from data+parity shards at ~1.2–1.8× overhead (ECC cited ~1.8× vs naive 3×) — cheaper at bulk scale, costlier CPU/network on repair.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares ~3× storage and fast repair vs ~1.2–1.8× ECC overhead and heavier repair.

must_hit.point: Interview default: replication for hot/small objects; ECC for bulk/cold durability — e.g. hot profile thumbnails vs 100 PB cold backups differ on overhead, repair cost, and latency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks replication for hot thumbnails and ECC/tiering for 100 PB cold backups with justification.

must_hit.point: Serving public/hot media needs CDN (and often Range requests) plus versioned or cache-busting keys; lifecycle policies move cold data to cheaper classes (IA/Glacier) or expire it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pairs object store with CDN for reads and mentions lifecycle tiering off hot Standard.

must_hit.point: Partition write load by key prefix; a single sequential prefix can absorb all writes — design keys for fan-out (or rely on store auto-sharding) in DIY systems.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out hot-prefix throughput and prefix fan-out in key design.

probes: For hot profile thumbnails versus 100 PB of cold backups, would you choose 3× replication or erasure coding, and why?

hints.1: Compare storage overhead and what happens when a disk fails.
hints.2: Hot/small wants fast repair and low latency; bulk cold wants lower bytes-on-disk.
hints.3: Thumbnails → replication (~3×, fast repair); 100 PB cold → ECC (~1.2–1.8×, heavier repair) plus colder storage classes.

phases.goal: Apply the S3 + metadata + CDN pattern to media upload, large-file sync, and a lite object-store design.

must_hit.point: Instagram-style photo upload: client → presigned PUT to S3 → notification/callback → metadata row in DB → CDN URL for reads; do not store JPEG in MySQL or stream every download through the API tier.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches presigned upload, metadata write, CDN read path, and rejects DB BLOB and API proxying.

must_hit.point: For an 8 GB video on flaky mobile: use multipart with per-part retry; if the client dies mid-upload, abort/GC orphaned parts rather than leaving incomplete assemblies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses the 8 GB flaky-network drill: initiate/parts/complete/abort and orphaned-part cleanup.

must_hit.point: Dropbox-style edit that changes 1% of a file should re-upload changed chunks only: chunk/block hashing, metadata mapping file → chunk IDs, and optional cross-user dedupe at a high level.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Avoids full-file re-upload; describes chunk IDs in metadata and hashing for dedupe.

must_hit.point: Lite design-S3 attack: requirements → estimate objects/QPS → PUT/GET/DELETE/LIST API → metadata service + chunk servers → durability (replication or ECC) → multipart → one deep dive (hot prefix, consistency, or GC of deleted objects).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Structures the answer with API, two planes, durability strategy, multipart, and one named deep dive.

probes: Design Instagram photo upload end-to-end, then say what changes for an 8 GB video upload and for a Dropbox file edit that only changes 1% of the bytes.

hints.1: Start from where bytes go and what the app DB stores.
hints.2: Presigned direct path for photos; multipart for multi-GB; chunk hashes for partial edits.
hints.3: Photo: presigned PUT → metadata → CDN; 8 GB: multipart + abort orphans; 1% edit: re-upload changed chunks only via file→chunk-ID metadata.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Replication (~3× storage) is simple with fast repair — prefer for hot/small. ECC (Reed–Solomon/LRC, ~1.2–1.8× overhead, ~1.8× vs naive 3×) saves capacity at cold/warm bulk scale but costs more CPU/network to repair.
Proxying GB through app servers for "security" is wrong; use short-lived presigned URLs/STS and enforce auth on the grant so the app stays control-plane.
Public/hot media should sit behind a CDN (and Range requests where useful) with versioned or cache-busting keys; origin alone is a poor geo-latency story.

Durability is not losing bytes (e.g. 11 nines via multi-AZ redundancy + scrubbing); availability is being reachable now; consistency is whether a read sees the latest write — modern S3 is strong RAWW for PUT/overwrite/DELETE, but do not assume every store.

gotchas.trap: Putting large blobs in the primary DB
gotchas.correction: Backups, replicas, and queries melt; use object store + thin metadata pointers.

gotchas.trap: Proxying uploads through app servers "for security"
gotchas.correction: Use short-lived presigned URLs/STS; still enforce auth when granting access.

gotchas.trap: Confusing durability with availability or consistency
gotchas.correction: Durability = won't lose data; availability = reachable now; consistency = read sees latest write — treat them separately.

gotchas.trap: Drawing S3 folders as real directories
gotchas.correction: They are key prefixes; LIST and permissions differ from a POSIX filesystem.
Single PUT risks timeouts and full restarts under network loss; use multipart with per-part retry (≥100 MB practice).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting CDN (or Range requests) on the public media read path
gotchas.correction: Origin S3 alone is the wrong geo latency story; pair with CDN and cache-busting/versioned keys.

gotchas.trap: Assuming every cloud blob store is eventually consistent forever
gotchas.correction: S3 is strongly consistent for object PUT/overwrite/DELETE now; state what your design guarantees.

gotchas.trap: Naive 3× replication of everything at EB scale
gotchas.correction: Interviewers expect ECC and tiering cost awareness for bulk/cold data.
